# Sizing a power station for a fridge

You need to check three things: surge, running watts, and watt-hours.

**1. Surge watts (the one that most often rules out a unit)**
- The compressor briefly draws about 2-3x its running watts when it starts.
- Sources put this at roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. A safe target is a surge or peak rating of at least **1,300 W**, higher for a large or older fridge ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
- Small units meant for phones and laptops often fail this check.

**2. Continuous watts**
- A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station covers it.
- Add up anything else you'll run at the same time.
- Choose a pure sine wave inverter.

**3. Watt-hours (how long it lasts)**
- The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so average draw is roughly 40-70 W.
- Your fridge's EnergyGuide label gives a better figure: kWh per year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = average watts.
- Estimated capacity needs, with inverter losses and some headroom:

| Outage length | Capacity needed |
|---|---|
| About half a day to ~17 hours | ~1,000 Wh |
| 24 hours | ~1,400-2,000 Wh |
| 2 days | ~2,800 Wh or more |

The sources differ a little. HomeGridHQ estimates a 1,070 Wh unit runs a fridge about 17 hours ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)). powerstations.reviews recommends about 1,400 Wh for a full day, which includes a 20% safety margin. Warm kitchens, frequent door openings, and large side-by-sides with ice makers push usage up. Keep the door shut during the outage.

## Options that fit

- **About 1,000 Wh (most of a day):**
  - BLUETTI AC180, 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W with 2,700 W peak, seen around $399-699 ([details](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
  - Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, about $499 per HomeGridHQ ([details](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- **About 1,400-1,500 Wh (a full day with a margin):** BLUETTI AC180P, 1,440 Wh, 1,800 W with 2,700 W surge, $649 at BLUETTI but sold out when checked Oct 15 ([details](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
- **About 2,000 Wh (a day and a half or more, plus a few other essentials):**
  - BLUETTI AC200L, 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W continuous, expandable up to 8 kWh. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which Dealectric tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-21. [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) (affiliate link; the [product page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) has full specs). It has 3,000+ cycles, fewer than some competitors.
  - Anker SOLIX S2000, 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W with 3,000 W peak, $699.99 after coupon ([Anker page](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)).

Prices change, so confirm at checkout. For most households, a **~1,500-2,000 Wh LiFePO4 station with at least 1,300 W of surge** is the safe pick for a 24-hour outage.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one model.
